$comment: PROTOTYPE, throwaway. Wayfinder ticket 20 on david/artemis (Forgejo). The suggestions catalogue Artemis would fetch at launch from its own repository, with the shipped copy as fallback. Two sections: skills (repositories a user can follow, whole or skill by skill) and instructions (standing prompts a user can tick to own a copy of). Nothing is pre-ticked: the user chooses. The generated Setup prompts are NOT catalogue entries: Artemis renders them from live facts; their draft texts live in prototype-suggestions-catalogue.html for review only. Revision 2 after David's review on 2026-09-22.

groups.title: Setup
groups.blurb: Written by Artemis from what you set up: your memory banks, your skills, your key manager. On by default once the feature is configured. Editable and removable like any other.

groups.title: Coding
groups.blurb: Habits for work in a repository. Read each and tick the ones you want.

groups.blurb: How the agent talks to you and delegates. Personal, so read each before ticking.

groups.title: Custom
groups.blurb: Your own. Anything you write here is yours from the start.

entries.title: Read code from a fresh checkout
entries.summary: Pull or clone before you reference code, and say which commit you read.
entries.text: Before you reference, quote or change code in a repository, make sure you are reading the current default branch: pull the latest from its remote, or clone it fresh into a scratch directory. Say which commit you read from. A stale checkout produces confident answers about code that no longer exists.

entries.title: Check a pull request is still open before pushing to it
entries.summary: A merged or closed PR gets a new branch and a new PR, not more commits.
entries.text: Before pushing further commits to a branch that has a pull request, check that the pull request is still open. If it has been merged or closed, do not push to that branch: start a new branch from the default branch and open a new pull request that links the old one.

entries.title: Read automated reviews after pushing
entries.summary: Wait for CI and any review bots, then answer or fix every comment before asking a person.
entries.text: After you push a pull request, wait for continuous integration and for any automated reviewers the repository runs (AI review bots, linters that comment). Read every comment they leave and either fix it or reply with why not, before you ask a person to review or before you merge. If the repository runs no automated reviewers, skip this. Never merge a pull request you were allowed to merge without checking for new automated review comments first.

entries.title: No attribution lines
entries.summary: No co-author trailers, no generated-by footers, no signature in PR descriptions.
entries.text: Do not add yourself as an author or co-author of commits, and do not append any generated-by, signed-off or attribution line to commit messages or pull request descriptions. The person you work for is the author of record.

entries.title: Ask with a recommended answer
entries.summary: Interactive question prompts, researched first, best option first.
entries.text: When you need a decision from me, ask through an interactive question prompt rather than in prose. Do enough research first to have a recommended answer, put that option first and mark it as recommended, and give each option a one-line consequence. Ask only what you cannot settle yourself.

entries.title: Which model runs your subagents
entries.summary: A default model and effort for delegated work. Fill in the placeholders before enabling.
entries.text: When you delegate work to subagents, run them on {model} at {effort} effort unless I say otherwise for a task. Name the model you used when you report what a subagent found.
